title: Other user accounts on this computer
whyItMatters: Every account on the machine can hold its own personal data. Listing the names shows whether someone else used this computer and may have left files behind.
source: FHS 3.0, /home: user home directories live under /home on Linux: https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch03s08.html
notes: Names only and never inside another profile. excludeHome keeps the scanning user out. Accounts without a home folder, or with homes elsewhere (LDAP, /var/home on immutable distros), are not listed.

cleanup.exportFirst: Have each other person copy their files off first, to an external drive or their own new computer.
steps: Look at the account names in the plan and decide which people still need theirs.
Ask each other person to take their files before anything is removed.
In Settings > System > Users, unlock, select the account, choose Remove User, then Delete Files. An administrator password is needed.
cleanup.risk: Deleting user accounts permanently removes their login access, personal files, and user configurations.
cleanup.source: GNOME Help, Delete a user account: https://help.gnome.org/users/gnome-help/stable/user-delete.html
